notes.title: Devlog #5: Visual Upgrades
notes.content: [p]Hello everyone! It's been 23 days since the last devlog, and today, on the 68th day of CaveVox development, I'll share the numerous changes that have taken place during this time.[/p][p] [/p][p][b]CaveVox Demo[/b][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3942210/CaveVox_Demo/"][/dynamiclink]The CaveVox Demo is scheduled for release in early October 2025. You can already add it to your wishlist and try it for free when it's released. In the demo, you'll be able to explore the first floors of the dungeon, get familiar with the gameplay, and immerse yourself in the game's atmosphere. The demo will be single-player only, and your feedback will be extremely important for further development.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Early Access[/b][/p][p]Early access is planned for Q4 2025. The game will cost $10 (less than the $12 release price) as a token of support for players. There will be no DLC — all updates will be added to the purchased game. Early access will include cooperative play with friends, as well as new dungeon levels featuring unique elements, monsters, and gameplay. Localization into multiple languages is planned — details will be available on the game pages.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Graphics and Visual Improvements[/b][/p][p]The game now looks visually smoother and more pleasant. Shaders, shadows, lighting, textures, and item models have been improved. For example, vines can now grow on the walls, and in the future, web generation and various item states will be added: intact, slightly damaged, and fully broken — depending on the dungeon level.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45040521/742f26b1cb7f37ac3baa070fcd31974fbd2dc3f6.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45040521/2f9b809f2ce78f313abb06ce4283bb452e70c730.png"][/img][/p][p]The rendering system has been completely rewritten, reducing hardware requirements. For example, invisible parts of the map are now culled.[/p][p]Item generation has become fast and predictable: objects are now placed on a grid, which is suitable for a voxel world and eliminates visual glitches.[/p][p]New types of rooms have also been added, with different sets for each dungeon level.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Sounds and Interface[/b][/p][p]Environmental sounds and SFX have been refined: attacks, jumps, running. The interface has also been updated: the map is now at the bottom left, and the character status is at the bottom right, freeing up space in front of the player and making controls more convenient.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="vKBG4aduIz0;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]This is just part of the changes — I'll cover many smaller updates in future devlogs. Thank you for reading until the end! Join our newly created [url="https://discord.gg/YPqBB68w9N"]Discord server[/url] to discuss the game.[/p]

notes.title: Devlog #4: Enemies
notes.content: [p]Hello everyone! Today is the 44th day of [b]CaveVox[/b] development. In this devlog, we will talk about the dungeon enemies. The early stages of development were shared outside of Steam, but now we’ll regularly share our progress here as well![/p][p]Monsters are a natural threat for any roguelike explorer. But CaveVox is not endless extermination of hordes, like in classic Action-RPGs. Here the player freely wanders through the dungeon floors, where not every room is filled with danger. Sometimes these can be barracks, dining halls, lobbies, or other rooms that change from floor to floor and create the feeling of a truly living world.[/p][p]The types of monsters partially overlap with [b][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1385180/Kingso/"]Kingso[/url][/b], but as a prequel, CaveVox also introduces unique enemies. The dungeon keeps its own secrets: it spawns its inhabitants, replenishes their losses, and maintains balance, allowing the depths to remain dangerous.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45040521/586aa7ecd34787cc0617b9cafba4f458a7d5a50f.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45040521/131f5358b75bf2810aedc16281f52a2e96f03d30.png"][/img][/p][p]Take, for example, the [b]water slime[/b] — the simplest and yet insidious enemy. It is a blue jelly-like substance whose strength and mobility directly depend on its mass. The slime moves by jumping, sticking and slapping against the floor and walls. A single enemy like this is easily defeated, but several together are capable of overcoming even a well-prepared party of adventurers.[/p][p]The placement of enemies fully depends on the dungeon generation. Earlier, the creation of rooms was already mentioned, but recently their structure was updated. Now the rooms have different shapes, connected into a dependency network, which makes every floor unique and unpredictable. The deeper you go, the more diverse and stronger the enemies become.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="69StWDrhD3Y;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]The difficulty of enemies also differs. It is planned that enemies will use vision, hearing, and object awareness based on a principle similar to occlusion culling for sound: walls, room geometry, and the placement of objects will affect what they can see, what they can hear, and which signals from objects (for example, noise from equipment, falling items, or active devices) can reveal the presence of the player or events. This system will allow them to naturally react to the environment, track targets by sound, account for interactive objects, and even coordinate group actions.[/p][p]Currently, audio occlusion is [b]already implemented[/b] and was described in a previous devlog: environmental and object sounds are correctly dampened and distorted by obstacles, making the dungeons feel truly atmospheric.[/p][p]Thank you for following the development of [b]CaveVox[/b] — every new day makes the dungeon deeper and more alive.[/p]
